proposed.text: An architect created distinctive building designs in 1990. The architect died in 2015. Under RA 8293, when does copyright in these works expire?

options.text: In 2040 (25 years after creation), which confuses ordinary architectural works with the separate applied-art term
In 2035 (20 years after creation), which is not the RA 8293 copyright term for this work
In 2065 (50 years after the architect's death under RA 8293 Section 213.1)
Copyright in architectural works never expires under Philippine law

rationale.a: This uses the 25-year applied-art rule instead of Section 213.1 for the stated individual architect.
rationale.d: RA 8293 gives a long term, not perpetual copyright.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 213.1 protects works under Sections 172 and 173 during the life of the author and for fifty years after death. The architect died in 2015, so the 50-year post-mortem period runs to 2065. The date of creation does not control this individual-author term.
rationale.takeaway: For individual architects, add 50 years to the author's death year.

proposed.explanation: Corrected the answer option from 2085/life plus 70 to 2065/life plus 50 under local RA 8293.
